company_name: Skydance Corporation (formerly Paramount Skydance Corporation; NYSE: SKYD, formerly Nasdaq: PSKY)
overview: Skydance Corporation is a global media and entertainment company formed on August 7, 2025 when David Ellison's Skydance Media acquired control of Paramount Global via a purchase of National Amusements, Inc. and a subsequent merger that combined Paramount Global and Skydance Media under a new holding company (originally named Paramount Skydance Corporation). On October 6, 2026 the company completed a second transformational acquisition -- Warner Bros. Discovery, Inc. (WBD) -- for roughly $31.00/share in cash (~$81 billion equity value, ~$97-110 billion including assumed/repaid debt), renamed itself Skydance Corporation, and began trading on the NYSE under ticker 'SKYD' (its predecessor traded as PSKY on Nasdaq). The combined company now owns Paramount Pictures, CBS, CBS News/Sports, Nickelodeon, MTV, BET, Comedy Central, Paramount+, Pluto TV and Skydance's film/animation/games/sports studios, together with Warner Bros., HBO/HBO Max, CNN, Warner Bros. Television, DC, TNT Sports, Cartoon Network, Food Network and HGTV. Pro forma annual revenue is roughly $70 billion, making it one of the largest content companies in the world, but it carries roughly $80-87 billion of gross debt as a result of the WBD acquisition financing.

business_model.summary: Revenue is earned through three channels: (1) advertising sold on broadcast/cable networks and ad-supported streaming; (2) affiliate/subscription fees (cable carriage, broadcast retransmission, and streaming subscriptions for Paramount+/HBO Max); and (3) content licensing, theatrical box office, and home entertainment. Streaming subscription revenue is recurring; advertising and theatrical revenue are transactional/cyclical and heavily influenced by tentpole events (Super Bowl rotation, elections, major film slates). Legacy Paramount reported under TV Media, Direct-to-Consumer, and Filmed Entertainment segments through 2025; beginning 2026 the segments were renamed TV Media, Direct-to-Consumer, and Studios (Filmed Entertainment plus TV studio operations combined). Post-WBD segment reporting for the combined entity has not yet been disclosed (initial purchase-accounting is incomplete; full pro forma segment detail is promised in the FY2026 10-K).

revenue_streams.name: TV Media (legacy Paramount: CBS, cable networks, int'l free-to-air, TV studios)
revenue_streams.trend: declining (pro forma -9% in FY2025 on linear ad/affiliate erosion)

revenue_streams.name: Direct-to-Consumer (Paramount+, Pluto TV, BET+)
revenue_streams.trend: growing (+12% pro forma FY2025; Paramount+ subs 78.9M, +4% YoY)

revenue_streams.name: Studios/Filmed Entertainment (Paramount Pictures, Skydance, Miramax)
revenue_streams.trend: volatile, release-slate dependent (-5% pro forma FY2025)

business_model.customer_type: B2C (streaming/pay-TV subscribers, theatrical moviegoers) and B2B (advertisers, MVPDs/distributors, content licensees)
business_model.geographic_mix: Predominantly U.S. (CBS Network, CBS Stations, domestic cable/streaming) with international free-to-air (Network 10 Australia, Channel 5 UK) and global Paramount+/HBO Max distribution; WBD adds substantial international HBO Max and Warner Bros. International Television footprint not yet broken out post-merger.

competitive_position.market_position: Following the WBD acquisition, Skydance becomes one of the two or three largest traditional media/streaming conglomerates by content library scale and revenue (~$70B pro forma), combining CBS's #1-rated broadcast network, the Paramount/Warner Bros. film libraries (Star Wars-tier IP such as Harry Potter, DC, Mission: Impossible, Transformers, Looney Tunes), and a combined Paramount+/HBO Max streaming base that management plans to bundle starting early 2027. Legacy linear TV Media remains in secular decline.

moat_factors.description: Combined library now includes Harry Potter, DC, HBO prestige TV, Mission: Impossible, Transformers, Titanic, Godfather, Star Trek, and CBS/Nickelodeon libraries -- very difficult to replicate

NFL (incl. AFC playoffs/rotational Super Bowl), NCAA Division I Men's Basketball Tournament, UEFA Champions League, Masters/PGA, plus WBD's TNT Sports rights (NBA, MLB, NHL, March Madness) create appointment viewing and affiliate leverage
29 owned CBS stations in top U.S. markets operate under FCC licenses that are costly/impossible for new entrants to replicate, though ownership caps also constrain Skydance's own M&A flexibility

Ellison family wealth (Lawrence and David Ellison) plus RedBird Capital, and sovereign wealth funds (Saudi PIF, Qatar Investment Authority, Abu Dhabi) provided tens of billions in PIPE equity to fund the WBD deal -- a capital-access advantage few media rivals have
Paramount+ (78.9M subs) plus HBO Max combine into a large bundled streaming base designed to compete on content depth with Netflix/Disney+

weaknesses: Linear TV Media (advertising + affiliate fees) in structural decline across both legacy Paramount and WBD assets
Extremely high leverage (~$80-87B gross debt) constrains strategic and capital-return flexibility versus less-levered peers (Disney, Netflix, Comcast)

Dual-class, 'controlled company' governance (Ellison family controls ~77.5% of voting Class A stock; Class B shareholders have no vote) limits minority shareholder influence and may depress valuation multiples
Integration of two large, culturally different organizations (Paramount/CBS, Skydance, and now WBD/HBO/CNN) within 15 months creates significant execution risk
Direct-to-Consumer segment has historically been unprofitable or barely profitable on a standalone Adjusted OIBDA basis (-$497M in FY2024, +$153M-$77M in 2025 periods)

growth_drivers: WBD acquisition cost synergies targeted at $6 billion run-rate within three years (net of reinvestment), including ~$1.4B of ~$4B technology spend, ~$1.0B of ~$5B marketing spend, and ~$2.2B from eliminating redundant back-office/corporate functions
Combined HBO Max + Paramount+ streaming bundle planned for launch in early 2027, aiming to improve subscriber retention/ARPU and compete more directly with Netflix and Disney+
Paramount+ subscriber and pricing growth (78.9M global subscribers at YE2025, +4% YoY; subscription revenue +20% pro forma in FY2025)
Deleveraging plan: management targets reducing leverage to ~3.0x by 2029 using excess free cash flow, which (if achieved) would materially re-rate the equity
Expanded sports rights portfolio (NFL, NCAA, UEFA, PGA/Masters from legacy Paramount plus NBA/MLB/NHL/March Madness via WBD's TNT Sports) as a streaming/linear differentiator
Potential for further portfolio rationalization (completed sales of Telefe-Argentina and Chilevisión-Chile in 2025/2026) and asset monetization to pay down debt

business.description: Combining Paramount/Skydance (itself barely 14 months into its own integration) with WBD -- a far larger, operationally distinct organization -- within a compressed timeframe risks cost-synergy shortfalls, talent attrition, and operational disruption

Broadcast/cable advertising and affiliate revenues are structurally declining industry-wide (TV Media pro forma revenue -9% in FY2025); WBD adds significant additional linear cable exposure (CNN, TNT, Cartoon Network, Food Network, HGTV) facing the same pressure
Direct-to-Consumer has only recently turned modestly profitable; achieving durable profitability across a combined, much larger Paramount+/HBO Max streaming business is unproven
AMPTP agreements with the WGA (expires May 2026) and DGA/SAG-AFTRA (expire June 2026) create renewed strike risk following the 2023 WGA/SAG-AFTRA strikes that disrupted production
Management flagged WBD theatrical underperformance will reduce Q4 2026 profit by up to ~$200 million versus prior expectations

financial.description: Gross debt rose from ~$15.0 billion at September 30, 2026 to roughly $87 billion post-WBD-close (per Q3 2026 earnings coverage), funded via ~$57B of new secured debt (Term B-1 Loans, First/Second Lien Senior Secured Notes, Term A loans) plus assumption/refinancing of WBD's debt; servicing this load materially constrains free cash flow

Skydance issued ~3,918 million new Class B shares at $12.00/share to equity syndication parties (Ellison, RedBird, Saudi PIF, Qatar Investment Authority, Abu Dhabi L'Imad, LionTree) to fund the deal, taking shares outstanding from ~1.1 billion to ~5.04 billion -- a ~4.5x increase

A large portion of the new debt stack and the junior subordinated debentures reset to floating/benchmark-linked rates over time; a 1% rate move was estimated (pre-WBD) to swing debt fair value by several hundred million dollars, and the effect is now much larger on the enlarged debt base

The company has continued paying a small quarterly dividend ($0.05-$0.10/share) despite the leverage increase; capital allocation priority is stated to be debt paydown toward a 3.0x leverage target by 2029, creating tension with the dividend and any buyback capacity

regulatory.description: Twelve state attorneys general sued to block the WBD deal (State of California et al. v. Paramount Skydance Corp. et al.); a States Consent Decree effective September 30, 2026 requires the combined company to comply with specified commitments (including formation of a 'News Editorial Independence Board' for CBS News/CNN) over a five-year commitment period, constraining editorial and possibly structural flexibility

National TV ownership cap (39% household reach) and local ownership rules, plus foreign ownership restrictions (25% voting/equity cap), could force station divestitures or limit future consolidation given the enlarged combined station group

GDPR/UK GDPR, U.S. state privacy laws, COPPA and children's-online-safety rules, and evolving AI-related IP/liability rules raise compliance costs across the much larger combined content and advertising operations

macro.description: Advertising revenue (still roughly a third of legacy Paramount's pro forma revenue) is sensitive to macro conditions, tariff-driven uncertainty, and election/sports cycle timing (Super Bowl rotation, NCAA Tournament biennial rights, political ad cycles)
With ~$80-87B of gross debt, the combined company is now one of the most rate-sensitive large-cap media names; a sustained higher-for-longer rate environment raises refinancing costs materially
International operations (Network 10, Channel 5, HBO Max international, Warner Bros. International TV) create euro/pound/other FX translation and hedging exposure

execution.description: David Ellison (Chairman/CEO) now shares operating leadership with newly appointed co-CEO Ynon Kreiz (ex-WBD/Mattel); dual-CEO structures carry governance and decision-speed risk during a critical integration period

Voluntary buyouts, a new five-day in-office policy, and layoffs (already including several senior executives from both legacy organizations, plus cuts in the games division) are underway; poorly managed restructuring risks talent flight and production disruption
Multiple lawsuits were filed challenging both the original Paramount-Skydance transaction and the WBD merger; adverse rulings could impose costs or operational constraints

macro_factors.industry_outlook: Legacy linear TV advertising and affiliate revenue continue to decline industry-wide as viewers shift to streaming; the WBD deal is explicitly a bet that scale, IP breadth, and bundled streaming (Paramount+ + HBO Max) can offset that decline and fund massive acquisition debt.
macro_factors.cyclicality: Moderate-to-high: advertising and theatrical revenues are cyclical and event-driven; subscription streaming revenue is more recurring but exposed to consumer discretionary spending and churn.
macro_factors.interest_rate_sensitivity: High -- the company is now one of the most debt-levered large media companies (~$80-87B gross debt), making both GAAP interest expense and refinancing risk highly sensitive to rates.
key_input_costs: Content/production costs (talent, writers, sports rights fees)

recent_developments.event: Skydance Media completed its acquisition of control of Paramount Global via the NAI Transaction and merged Paramount Global and Skydance Media into new holding company Paramount Skydance Corporation (PSKY on Nasdaq); Ellison family became controlling stockholder (~77.5% of Class A voting stock)
Paramount Skydance launched an unsolicited $30.00/share cash tender offer for Warner Bros. Discovery, competing against WBD's existing agreed merger with Netflix

Raised offer to $31.00/share, added a quarterly 'ticking fee,' and increased the regulatory break fee to $7.0 billion; WBD board found the proposal could constitute a 'Company Superior Proposal' versus the Netflix deal

States Consent Decree with twelve state attorneys general (resolving litigation over the deal) took effect, permitting the WBD merger to close subject to five-year behavioral commitments including a News Editorial Independence Board

Completed the ~$81 billion (equity)/ ~$97-110 billion (incl. debt) acquisition of Warner Bros. Discovery; renamed the company Skydance Corporation; began trading as 'SKYD' on the NYSE; issued ~3,918 million new Class B shares at $12.00/share to Ellison/RedBird/sovereign-wealth syndication investors; repaid WBD's $14.7B term loans; gross debt rose to roughly $87 billion

Reported Q3 2026 earnings (first report since the WBD close, though WBD results are not yet consolidated): revenue ~$7.0 billion (+5% YoY), net earnings of $73 million (swing to profit), Paramount+ revenue +21-20%; announced $6 billion three-year run-rate synergy target and a leverage target of 3.0x by 2029; guided Q4 2026 profit down by up to $200 million due to WBD theatrical underperformance; stock fell more than 8% on the report

Post-close analyst reaction mixed-to-negative: Bank of America maintained Underperform and cut its target from $13 to $11; Wells Fargo-style peers (Creutz) at Hold/$8; MoffettNathanson Neutral/$7; Guggenheim Neutral with no target citing lack of pro forma WBD disclosure; stock trading in the high-single digits, well below pre-close trading levels

Integration actions underway: voluntary employee buyouts, new five-day return-to-office policy, several senior executives (4 ex-WBD, 4 ex-Paramount) departed, layoffs in the games division (Skydance Interactive/Paramount Games); combined HBO Max/Paramount+ bundle planned for early 2027

guidance.fiscal_year: FY2026 (transition year post-WBD close) / medium-term through 2029

items.notes: Against an expense base of >$50B; breakdown: ~$1.4B of ~$4B technology spend, ~$1.0B of ~$5B marketing spend, ~$2.2B from redundant back-office/corporate function elimination; supersedes the earlier ~$2B Paramount-Skydance-only synergy target
Management stated excess free cash flow will be directed to debt repayment until this target is reached, following the leverage spike from the WBD financing

items.target: reduced by up to $200 million versus prior expectations
items.notes: Driven by theatrical underperformance at the newly acquired Warner Bros. Studios slate
Key product initiative to retain/cross-sell the combined streaming subscriber base

items.target: up to ~$800 million (Paramount-Skydance integration only, pre-WBD)
items.notes: Disclosed in the FY2025 10-K; does not yet include incremental WBD integration costs, which have not been separately quantified

guidance.management_commentary: CEO David Ellison and newly appointed co-CEO Ynon Kreiz have emphasized that scale and combined IP/sports rights, alongside aggressive cost synergies, are intended to offset linear decline and fund paydown of the debt taken on for the WBD acquisition; management has acknowledged further layoffs are coming but has not disclosed a total headcount reduction figure. The pro forma financial statements and segment detail for the combined WBD entity will not be available until the FY2026 Form 10-K given the limited time between the October 6, 2026 close and the Q3 2026 filing.

bull_case: Combined content library (Paramount/CBS/Skydance plus Warner Bros./HBO/DC/CNN) is one of the deepest and most valuable in media, with ~$70B of pro forma revenue and significant sports rights breadth
$6 billion targeted run-rate synergies, if delivered, would be transformative relative to the combined cost base and could materially improve margins and free cash flow available for deleveraging

Deep-pocketed backers (Ellison family, RedBird Capital, Saudi PIF, Qatar Investment Authority, Abu Dhabi investment vehicles) provide a capital cushion and signal long-term conviction uncommon among media peers

Stock has sold off sharply post-close (high single digits versus a $31/share WBD deal price), potentially pricing in excessive pessimism if integration and deleveraging execute reasonably well, with some analysts (Benchmark $19, Guggenheim $14 pre-close) seeing material upside

Combined HBO Max + Paramount+ streaming bundle (launching early 2027) could improve retention/pricing power versus standalone services and help the Direct-to-Consumer segment reach sustainable profitability at scale
bear_case: Extreme leverage (~$80-87 billion gross debt against a company only recently OIBDA-positive) leaves little room for error; a shortfall in synergy delivery or a cyclical ad/theatrical downturn could strain debt service and force a dividend cut or dilutive refinancing

Integration risk is compounding: the company is simultaneously finishing the Paramount-Skydance integration (begun August 2025) while absorbing a WBD organization that is larger than Paramount itself, within roughly 14 months

Massive share issuance (~3.9 billion new Class B shares at $12.00) nearly quintupled the share count, diluting existing holders and making per-share value creation dependent on very large absolute synergy/FCF gains

Structural decline in linear TV advertising and affiliate fees now affects a much larger combined cable/broadcast footprint (CBS, CNN, TNT, Cartoon Network, Food Network, HGTV, Network 10, Channel 5), and the States Consent Decree's News Editorial Independence Board and other commitments constrain operational flexibility for five years

Dual-class governance (Ellison family controls ~77.5% of voting power; Class B public shareholders have no vote) and 'controlled company' exemptions reduce minority shareholder protections and can depress the valuation multiple the market is willing to pay, as reflected in the stock's post-close decline and predominantly Hold/Underperform analyst ratings
